html:
The Four Luna River Free Cities: Menibór, Napesbay, Bluehart and Bellacaire

Region in the English ranking survey: Empire of Anbennar (EoA).

Four one-province free cities, four civic personalities, sharing a path from post-war survival to a league of Luna River city-states. Choose Menibór for adventurers and mercenaries; Napesbay for a harbour and fleet; Bluehart for diplomacy and Damerian heritage; or Bellacaire for neutrality, fortifications and refuge for the displaced.

Local version: v1.37.5.0. Each city has 20 shared Luna River missions and 2 country-specific missions. Forming Pashainé (B59) replaces these with the successor's mission tree. The survey groups the four cities into entry 24, so they share this article; they remain four distinct Tags and receive separate personality-test results.

Four Cities After the War

In 1444, Menibór (A55), Napesbay (A82), Bluehart (A61) and Bellacaire (Z03) are republican free cities within the Empire of Anbennar, following the Regent Court and holding one province apiece. What the Fourth Lilac War left them was not a shared victory, but the memory of armies repeatedly crossing the valley and cities bearing the costs of princely ambitions. Menibór's history file explicitly records a Rose Party background, and Bluehart's a Moon Party background; these affiliations should not be imposed on Napesbay or Bellacaire without equivalent evidence. They compete with one another, but face the same problem: preserving autonomy between the emperor and powerful local neighbours.

Starting city Historical background and civic character Direction of its two unique missions Best suited to
Menibór A55 A Vernman city of adventurers; the Loop tavern, mercenary companies, anti-magic wards and the dwarven Riverstone Clan shape its civic memory Gather adventurers and mercenaries; refurbish the Loop Players who want mercenaries, personal networks and trade to sustain a small state
Napesbay A82 A Vernman city at the mouth of the Pírluna; the old Vernid arsenal, fleets and vineyards define its maritime identity Build the Napesfleet; restore the arsenal Players who want to begin with a harbour, light ships and the burgher estate
Bluehart A61 An East Damerian city preserving the traditions of Dameria's 21st Legion and the Hartlord Reassure neighbouring states; reorganise officers and the civic militia Players who enjoy diplomacy, negotiation and steady city-state development
Bellacaire Z03 An East Damerian fortress city that maintained its freedom through neutrality, fortifications and tolerance after repeated struggles for control Organise religious envoys; fortify the walls and provide civic relief Players who enjoy defence, alliances and protecting displaced people

These differences come from the four countries' ideas, history files and unique missions; they do not mean that the shared missions are entirely different. The academy mentioned in Bluehart's ideas was founded in 1604, while Bellacaire's Pink Stripe relief organisation develops along its mission route. Neither is an already completed institution in 1444.

The Shared Story: Turning Civic Influence into Imperial Leverage

The four cities begin by repairing wartime damage, stabilising civic life and winning imperial favour. A free-city starting event unlocks the Luna River Sway variable (the influence resource described in the Chinese article) and related burgher privileges. Agendas, missions and other activities increase Sway; decisions spend it on protection, civic status, trade rights and Luna River affairs. This is not another name for diplomatic power: it is a separate mechanism through which a single-city state turns court connections into regional leverage.

The shared missions then encourage the release or support of cities controlled by princes, coordination of subjects and allies, and investment in trade, industry, art, universities and urban infantry. Wars still occur, but the story is more concerned with sustaining the cities' common interests after the fighting. The closing mission, "Curtain Call", moves a loose league towards a common Pashainé identity: Damerian blue and Vernman red can become the "people of the purple river". This is a future mission-tree development, not an existing state at the start.

Each city's unique opening offers a different way forward. Menibór turns adventurer rosters, mercenaries and the Loop into civic defence and intelligence networks; friendship with Verne and adventurer companies is a mission reward, not an existing alliance in 1444. Napesbay establishes a fleet with light ships and an admiral, then restores the old arsenal's production and coastal defences. Bluehart draws on the old legion, noble officers and the Hartlord's traditions to organise its militia while repairing relations with Damerian states. Bellacaire uses religious envoys to cultivate goodwill, then makes its fortress a place of refuge through walls, taxation and civic relief. Their differences lie mainly in those two unique missions, starting geography and ideas—not four unrelated grand campaigns.

Four Historical Paths

Menibór's ideas recall how outside powers repeatedly tried to control the city after the decline of the Damerian Republic, only to be driven out by adventurer companies. Magisters and knights fighting the Wars of Rule clashed outside its walls, encouraging the defenders to develop anti-magic wards. Bridges across the river and the lively Loop made dwarves, merchants and mercenaries part of the city's story. Its mayor in 1444 is Rogier of Oldtower. Of the four cities, it has the strongest atmosphere of an adventurers' gathering place.

Napesbay is not an ordinary inland city on the main Luna. The offline English Wiki's Pírluna River article places it at the delta of a smaller river: vineyards and a prosperous valley attract minor nobles and retired adventurers, although commercial shipping is less substantial than at larger ports. The current local ideas also describe the old Vernid arsenal, precautions against pirates, and the secondary imperial fleet detained during the Lilac Wars to avoid making the city a target for the Rose Party. It is better understood as a neighbouring free city participating in Luna politics through its harbour and coastal defence.

Bluehart preserves the memory of Dameria's 21st Legion and the Hartlord. The military camp later became more than a symbol of armed strength: it also hosted negotiations, reflecting the city's preference for persuading powerful neighbours to stop. This does not mean a lack of military preparation; its unique missions still require an officer system and manpower in the capital. The ruler recorded in its history file in 1440 has undesirable personal traits. Those traits do not establish that the country's diplomatic ideal was already a virtue of that individual ruler.

Bellacaire's ideas tell the history of Bellac's Rock, originally a Vernman fortress that changed hands before the city increasingly relied on neutrality agreements and strong walls to remain free. The Battle of the Salt and Lance during the Lilac Wars commemorates its refusal to submit to invading armies. It is not a peaceful state that "never fights": its central concern is preserving defensible civic boundaries in wartime. The later mission-route network for helping displaced people continues that defensive history.

Forming Pashainé and Choosing a Personality

All four can follow the shared Luna River route and form Pashainé, B59 after completing the closing mission and meeting the formation decision's requirements for city numbers, administrative technology, peace and other conditions. The decision changes Tag and swaps non-generic missions. A special league branch can integrate some subjects; it cannot be summarised as "all vassals are automatically absorbed". This article evaluates the four starting countries' prelude, not B59's later imperial politics and conflicts as if they had already occurred under the predecessors.

Country v2.1 personality coordinates v2.1 values Why choose it
Menibór E42 · A25 · M/T50 I27 · P75 Good 81/100 Values autonomy, development and alliances, while readily using mercenaries and political bargaining to seek leadership.
Napesbay E37 · A25 · M/T50 I15 · P65 Good 73/100 Uses coastal defence, fleets and commercial privileges to survive; its practical aims are not centred on conquest or redemption.
Bluehart E35 · A20 · M/T50 I15 · P75 Good 85/100 Uses negotiation to restrain stronger powers and sustain civic autonomy, while keeping necessary military preparations; the assessment concerns the country's route, not an individual officeholder.
Bellacaire E29 · A20 · M/T50 I17 · P80 Good 90/100 Centres neutrality, alliances, fortifications and help for displaced people; defending the city can still require force.

Community comparisons often recommend Bluehart as a convenient first campaign: players consider its location, development base and unique rewards favourable. Napesbay's harbour creates a different opening, Bellacaire emphasises defence and diplomacy, and Menibór leans towards mercenaries. Others consider the four broadly similar and note waiting periods in the shared midgame. These are player experiences from 2025–2026, not definitive statements about current mechanics or difficulty.

Evidence Boundaries

Local history, ideas, missions and Chinese localisation establish the four identities and current gameplay. The three city homepages mentioned in the Chinese article's summary are short and mainly confirm free-city status; the Pírluna River and Luna River related pages provide more geographical context. Official developer diaries explain the Luna mission design and B59's intended continuation; Reddit player posts are experience sources only. The ranking sheet's Chinese spelling for Napesbay differs from the current localisation, which uses 纳普斯湾. The original English idea calls Bellacaire's battle "Battle of the Salt and Lance", where the Chinese article uses a name literally referring to salt and guns; the English version retains the verified original term without changing the Chinese research source. For detailed sources and the historical/future boundary, see the research evidence page.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when that set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as idea groups are filled, and the ambition applies after all seven have been unlocked. Only national ideas themselves are listed: racial, government and mission rewards are not mixed into their numbers, and a successor's new ideas do not automatically stack with the old ones. Descriptions may recall history or portray future ideals; they do not automatically describe events already completed in 1444.

Descriptions below use the native English localisation, not a back-translation of the Chinese localisation's occasionally expanded wording and quotations. Displayed effect values are retained from the Chinese research data; inherited unit discrepancies are explicitly qualified rather than silently corrected.

Menibór (A55) — Menibórian Ideas

Traditions: Menibórian Traditions

Effects: Mercenary Discipline: +5%; Trade Efficiency: +10%; May Recruit Female Generals: Allowed.

Idea 1: City of Valor

Menibór is second only to Anbenncóst itself in terms of how many adventurers hail from our city. From Derwing to Aiscestir, hopeful heroes of the Eastern Dameshead and beyond flock to our inns and taverns to begin their lives as adventurers, forming powerful and prestigious companies such as the Menibór Free Company in the process.

Effects: Mercenary Maintenance: -20%; Mercenary Cost: -20%.

Idea 2: Arcane Wards

During the Wars of Rule, the Magisters of Oldtower and the knights of Valiant Keep frequently clashed near our city, their magics risking the integrity of our walls on several occasions. To deal with them, small anti-magic wards were created to be mounted on the walls and worn by our warriors, allowing them to properly defend Menibór from the arcane chaos spreading around her.

Effects: shock_damage_received: -10%.

Idea 3: Bridgewine and Boar

Nothing soothes a tired adventurer more than a serving of Bridgewine with a hefty sausage!

Known more professionally as simply 'Menibór', it is a moderately strong red wine that is known for its spicy notes and high acidity - and has found strong favor amongst the bolder characters of Cannor.

Effects: Production Efficiency: +10%.

Idea 4: The Free City

Ever since the fall of the Damerian Republic our city has been one that few can manage to hold onto for long. Several times Damerian and Vernman forces alike were banished from the city by the adventurer companies and embroiled in bloody wars to reclaim her. Even though we've settled into the Empire, our neighbors know well the lengths a Menibórian will go to for our continued autonomous status.

Effects: Morale of Armies: +10%.

Idea 5: In The Loop

The Loop is the most famed tavern in the Luna Basin, only catering to the most legendary heroes, who frequently gather there to discuss happenings and glories abroad. The proprietors of the establishment are quick to inform us of anything of note that they hear, always ensuring the reach of our city council remains in The Loop.

Effects: Spy Network Construction: +10%; global_spy_defence: +10%.

Idea 6: Riverstone Clan

The dwarves of the Riverstone Clan were hired long ago to construct the many bridges that cross the Luna in our city, and they stayed behind to maintain them. As the city grew around their homes and workshops they expanded their influence, constructing virtually every structure in Menibór and operating as the city's primary architects and engineers to this day.

Effects: Construction Cost: -10%.

Idea 7: Hall of the Gallant

The dream of every adventurer from Menibór is to have their statues and names featured in the hallowed corridors of the Hall of the Gallant, a vast memorial dedicated to those heroes that lost their lives fighting for glory and justice. With names and busts dating back to before the Dragonwake, it is the most well known and respected edifice in the city.

Effects: Prestige: +1.

Ambition: Menibórian Ambition

Effects: Republican Tradition: +0.3.

Pashainé (B59) — Pashainéy Ideas

Traditions: Pashainéy Traditions

Effects: Legitimacy: +1; Devotion: +1; Republican Tradition: +0.3; Horde Unity: +1; Trade Steering: +20%.

Idea 1: Friends in High Places

“The greatest rulers preside not over a mere reign but an Era, a period which eclipses those ahead and behind in its profundity and prolificity. They understand that the legacy of the patron is his clients.” Tomás of Vallusna, ‘The Statesman’

Effects: Estate Interaction Cooldown Modifier: -10%; Administrative Advisor Cost: -25%.

Idea 2: Damerian Renaissance

“The imitation of style necessitates the imitation of form, and therefore of function. When we build a colonnade inspired by the formal markets of Old Dameria, we are inspired also by the conversation held along that colonnade, the type of life enabled by the structure we seek to recreate. The rhetorical tradition, the vibrant public life, even the raucous protest – all are made possible by the decision, made once again, to build space for them.” Saman of Fowlbarn, ‘The Life Of Stone’

Effects: Monthly Splendour: +1; Idea Cost: -10%.

Idea 3: Guild Philosophy

“Even in those realms which had not subordinated their government to an association of guild-backed aldermen, the Guild had been the fundamental unit of urban life in the Eastern Dameshead long before Pashainé’s emergence as a coherent state.

This had three major consequences. First, the codification of a sort of corporate democracy, a belief that society was best forged under a competing set of mutually-exerted pressures, by groups representing collectives of the population - even if these were subject to a monarch or a so-called ’Executive Guild’. Second, an emphasis on economic prosperity, the brass tacks ‘shopkeeper diplomacy’ for which Pashainé became notorious. Third, a relentless focus on urbanisation and the vertical integration of industry.” Silvard Dove, ‘An Economic History of Cannor’

Effects: Primary Culture Development Cost: -15%.

Idea 4: Blended Identity

“The poet Milian said that the Pashainéy is uniquely noble, having inherited the bravery of his Vernman father and the dignity of his Damerian mother. As a second daughter, I seem to have been left with the libido and stubbornness.” Genaia ‘Geni’ Cadesna sina Bellacaire, ‘Memoirs Of A Fallen Countess’

Effects: Free Policies: +1.

Idea 5: Cradle of Ravelianism

“Consider the conflict between Corinism and the Court which had so split the Valley. Consider, then, an unusually literate and engaged populace with a political impetus to see theological ruptures healed. Consider finally the Ravelian Lodge, which in its structure mimics the voluntary association basis of the guild. No population on Halann was more ready to embrace not merely the articles of belief but the basic organisational structure of Ravelianism.” Leande Bellac, ‘Apologetics’

Effects: Institution Spread in True Faith Provinces: +20%; Papal Influence: +2.

Idea 6: Birthplace of Protest

“Over the course of the eighteenth century, the slowly aggregating impact of the Verdancy became more and more clear across the entire Luna watershed. Land which had once been among the most fertile in Cannor gave harvest perhaps once in two years, while the concomitant soil pollution devastated the Valley’s few remaining natural forests. The result was an exodus of the population from the countryside and an even greater urbanisation of Pashainé, inadvertently birthing a contentious café and street culture; this would dominate the labour politics of the following hundred years, erupting again and again into civil unrest. You will find few along the Valley who have much to say in praise of Camir Silmuna, but our land is indelibly marked by his legacy.” Lucas síl Bellacaire, The History of the Lilac River, Vol. II

Effects: Morale of Armies: +10%.

Idea 7: Fallen and Remembered

“Do not fear death, my people. Fear nothing which you do in the company of brave souls; fear nothing which you do among your fellow citizens! We live in the time of the Mage-Emperors – in the era of the staff – and its power seems absolute. But we know these mages can die.

We knew it three hundred years ago, when the discipline of the fusillade first began to rival the arc of the fireball. We knew it two hundred years ago, when first we learned of that glorious substance, then accessible only so very far away, which could countermand their unearned gifts. And we know it now – now that their ritual of growth, their promise of endless harvest, has wrought a desolate steppe where once there was only verdant life. It is what they do! Addle the land, poison the water, wreck the bountiful Halann we share for the slightest chance at a lonely throne.

Hear me! It’s true – we may die today. But we die together, while they die alone.” Carric of Paredocks, Final Address

Effects: Land Leader Shock: +1.

Ambition: Pashainéy Ambition

Effects: National Tax Modifier: +20%.

Napesbay (A82) — Napesbayer Ideas

Traditions: Napesbayer Traditions

Effects: Sailors Modifier: +15%; Morale of Navies: +10%.

Idea 1: Vernid Arsenal

To prevent complete Damerian domination of the seas the old kingdom of Verne had established a bustling arsenal in Napesbay. Though the kingdom might've fallen long ago the infrastructure still stands, allowing us to continue producing vessels at a rapid rate, albeit under a different liege.

Effects: Shipbuilding Time: -20%; Ship Cost: -5%.

Idea 2: Brigand's Bane

Pirates of the Damesneck know to steer clear of Napesbayer vessels, for many a villainous corsair has been sent the sea floor by our guns over the centuries.

Effects: Galley Combat Ability: +10%.

Idea 3: Napesfleet

For centuries Napesbay was the home of the secondary Imperial fleet, frequently referred to as the Napesfleet, mirroring Neckcliffe across the Damesneck. When the Lilac Wars came roaring however, we knew that the fleet would only serve to make us a target should it remain in the hands of the Emperor. Thus, when the order came for the ships to leave port our officials seized the ships, declaring them property of the city and chasing down the ones that attempted to flee. While the Silmuna were understandably upset, bigger problems drew their attention from us and the fleet of Neckcliffe served well in our stead.

For most of the conflict anyway.

Effects: Naval Force Limit Modifier: +15%; Chance to Capture Enemy Ships: +10%.

Idea 4: Pírluna Vineyards

Along the gentle and slow-moving Pírluna are vineyards and wineries, tranquil slices of land owned by retired adventurers from Menibór. With a countryside more akin to the estate of a Wine Lord, they're one of the main employers in Napesbay, only after the arsenal and the navy.

Effects: Goods Produced Modifier: +10%.

Idea 5: Napesbay Company

Ruben of Napesbay was a daring and dashing captain, who led the colonial efforts of Verne, becoming one of the most famous explorers in Cannor. He of course didn't forget his home city, returning with gold and silver to establish a new colonial trading company in Napesbay, bringing trade from Aelantir back home.

Effects: Global Trade Power: +10%.

Idea 6: Gems in the Rough

Many of the pirate captains the captains of Napesbay captures are quite skilled, and it would be a waste to not make use of their talents. By establishing a rehabilitation program we can turn these rowdy raiders into proud admirals of the Napesfleet, fighting to finally rid the sea of their former comrades.

Effects: Naval Leader Fire: +2.

Idea 7: Rise of Napesbay

With the Napesbay Company running well and the Napesfleet keeping the seas clear of piracy, Napesbay has swiftly grown into one of the most prominent ports in the Damesneck. Many of the adventurers and settlers flocking to Aelantir leave Cannor through our city, and countless more have been moving here to establish new businesses, at home and abroad. Truly, this is Napesbay's golden age.

Effects: Development Cost: -10%.

Ambition: Napesbayer Ambition

Effects: Merchants: +1.

Bluehart (A61) — Blueharter Ideas

Traditions: Blueharter Traditions

Effects: Diplomatic Reputation: +200% (inherited source display; script raw value is diplomatic_reputation = 2, not a verified percentage conversion); Development Cost: -10%.

Idea 1: Tempering Ambition

Bluehart has always been surrounded by ambitious lords, eager to feast upon the riches of the Luna. Many a would-be conqueror have been turned away from our city, though not through the sword, but through the power of words. Our officials are experts in negotiating peace and reconciliation even with the most belligerent warlords, keeping our people safe from the horrors of combat.

Effects: Improve Relations: +20%.

Idea 2: Legacy of the Hartlord

Our city was originally founded as a legionary camp of the 21st Legion of Dameria, also known as the Legion XXI Hart. When the Republic fell to the Dragonwake, the former commander took control of the situation, allowing panicked civilians to flock to his protection and enforcing stability across the suddenly lawless frontier. In time he became known as The Hartlord, a paragon of peace and law, and when the Kingdom of Dameria rose from the ashes of the Republic, he readily submitted the new city of Bluehart to their rule, dying in his sleep as peacefully as he reigned. We hope to continue his legacy, acting as a force for goodwill despite whatever horrors wrack the lands around us.

Effects: Stability Cost Modifier: -15%.

Idea 3: Heart of the Luna

With the exception of Port Munas, our city is the largest on the Luna River. A prime destination for trade flowing downstream from the Wexhills, Blueharter merchants have little trouble finding markets to trade with from the comfort of home.

Effects: Global Trade Power: +10%.

Idea 4: Cymcestir

The old legion camp is known as the Cymcestir, though it hasn't been used for its original wartime purposes for quite some time. Ever since the reign of The Hartlord, the compound has been used as a diplomatic complex, providing comforting accommodations for foreign dignitaries and secure rooms for tense negotiations.

Effects: Diplomatic Relations: +1.

Idea 5: Sons of the XXI

Each member tracing direct lineage to the soldiers of the Legion XXI Hart, the Sons of the XXI are the brave sentinels of Bluehart, they alone are permitted to bear arms within city limits. They're said to fight with the ferocity of ten men each, determined to safeguard the city their ancestors fought for, that their children will grow up in, and that their descendants will continue to defend.

Effects: Infantry Combat Ability: +10%.

Idea 6: City of Tranquility

While turmoil brews around the city, none reaches past our city gates. Within the city is an atmosphere of tranquility, largely untouched by whatever calamity plagues the rest of the Empire.

Effects: National Unrest: -2.

Idea 7: Olóiegéanur Academy

The Cymcestir was expanded and converted into the Olóiegéanur Academy in 1604 as a result of simmering tensions within the fabric of Anbennar. The professors of the establishment find great gratification in training the next generation of statesmen and emissaries to act as agents of peace, ready to mend broke bridges across the Empire and assist in healing the wounds of the past.

Effects: Diplomats: +1.

Ambition: Blueharter Ambition

Effects: National Tax Modifier: +10%.

Bellacaire (Z03) — Bellacairey Ideas

Traditions: Bellacairey Traditions

Effects: Fort Maintenance: -15%; Production Efficiency: +10%.

Idea 1: Bellac's Rock

The most unique and storied structure of Bellacaire is the looming fortress of Bellac's Rock, first built by the King of Verne, Bellac Vernid, in 587 AA as a border fortress against Dameria. For centuries it stood against the ambitions of the north, up until it was seized from the Vernids in 917 AA, acting as a bastion against her original owners until it came under siege and occupation during the War of the Sorcerer-King. Despite its long and tumultuous history, Bellac's Rock is as sturdy as ever, a mighty citadel that continues to guard the lands around it.

Effects: Fort Defence: +20%.

Idea 2: Free City Confederation

When the winds of war blew across the Upper Luna, Bellacaire organized a neutrality pact with her fellow Free Cities of the river. Though it was ultimately short lived, the brief moment of unity along the Luna is a goal every Bellacairey hopes to replicate, to forge a realm strong enough to protect itself from being pulled into the conflicts of others.

Effects: Stability Cost Modifier: -15%.

Idea 3: Battle of the Salt and Lance

Despite our city's declared neutrality in the Lilac Wars, in the final days of the conflict she became the site of a brutal, yet inspiring, battle. The treacherous Cestiranders, recently supporters of the Rose Party, charged towards the city while the Galéinni did the same, both powers seeking to seize Bellacaire for their own ambitions. They met outside our gates, clashing in bloody melee while our own warriors took the field to defend the city. After four days and three nights, the invading forces were both forced to withdraw, for the guard of Bellacaire had ensured she would continue to stand free.

Effects: Morale of Armies: +10%; Prestige: +0.5.

Idea 4: Lunawalk

Running along the Luna River, the Lunawalk is where most Damerians settled after the fall of Bellac's Rock, establishing a patrician district along the gentle and serene banks. Far from reach of the great shadow cast by the Rock and gently lit by the moon at night, it is the most prestigious neighborhood in the city.

Effects: Prestige Decay: -1%.

Idea 5: The Drabsburd

On the other side of the city, far from the opulent abodes of the Lunawalk, the workshops and laboratories of the Drabsburd buzz and churn night and day. The strange gadgets and trinkets produced by the gnomes of the district are awe-inspiring to the populace, and the city government largely leaves the gnomes to innovate and invent at will, so long as they enforce safe practices and procedures.

Effects: Innovativeness Gain: +0.5; Idea Cost: -10%.

Idea 6: Impartial in Heavens and Halann

In the end, it truly doesn't matter who rests upon the throne of the Regent Court, for all of us shall know for sure when we pass from this world. Here one can find Adeanics and Corinites living in peace, free from the dogmatic hatred that drives their religious compatriots to battle outside the city.

Effects: Tolerance of Heretics: +2.

Idea 7: Pink Stripe

The horrors of the war between the Corinite and Adeanic Leagues has left countless refugees and orphans in its wake, and the majority of the Empire is content to let them suffer in silence. This will not stand for us. The Pink Stripe is an organization based in Bellacaire to assist and nurture those devastated by war and disaster, regardless of creed, allegiance, race, or otherwise. Already they've established charters across Anbennar, looking after those that have been left behind.

Effects: Diplomatic Reputation: +200% (inherited source display; script raw value is diplomatic_reputation = 2, not a verified percentage conversion).

Ambition: Bellacairey Ambition

Effects: Garrison Size: +0.3.
